elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement to an affiliate without Vendor consent.
elements.evidence: The clause permits Company to assign the Agreement “without Contractor's consent, to an affiliate.” The additional written-notice condition does not require consent.

elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement to a successor in connection with a merger without Vendor consent.
elements.evidence: The Company carve-out expressly covers assignment to a successor in connection with a merger without Contractor consent.

elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement to a successor in connection with an acquisition without Vendor consent.
elements.evidence: The Company carve-out expressly covers assignment to a successor in connection with an acquisition without Contractor consent.

elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement to a successor in connection with a sale of substantially all of its assets without Vendor consent.
elements.evidence: The Company carve-out covers assignment to a successor in connection with a sale of “all or substantially all of its assets” without Contractor consent.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign the Agreement without Customer's prior written consent.
elements.evidence: The opening sentence requires the other party's “express, prior written consent” for assignment, and no Vendor assignment exception is added.

elements.element: Customer may not unreasonably withhold consent to a Vendor assignment.
elements.evidence: The mutual consent requirement expressly states that consent “will not be unreasonably withheld.”

elements.element: Vendor may never assign or transfer the Agreement to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: The clause provides absolutely that “Contractor shall not assign or transfer this Agreement to any competitor of Company,” without a consent exception.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate the Agreement because of a Customer change of control.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly states that no Company change of control gives Contractor any right to terminate the Agreement or a Statement of Work.

elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement to a successor without Vendor consent.
elements.evidence: Company may assign without Contractor consent to a successor in connection with a merger, acquisition, reorganization, or sale of all or substantially all assets.

elements.element: Customer must provide Vendor written notice of an assignment to a successor.
elements.evidence: The permitted Company assignment to a successor is expressly conditioned on written notice to Contractor.

elements.element: Vendor may assign the Agreement to a successor without Customer consent.
elements.evidence: No equivalent successor-assignment exception is provided for Contractor; Contractor remains subject to Company's prior written consent.

elements.element: Vendor must provide Customer written notice of an assignment to a successor.
elements.evidence: The written-notice provision applies only to Company's permitted assignments to affiliates or successors. No Contractor successor notice mechanism is included.

elements.element: Customer assignments other than assignments to a successor require Vendor consent.
elements.evidence: The clause also permits Company to assign to an affiliate without Contractor consent, even though an affiliate assignment need not be an assignment to a successor.

elements.element: Vendor may not unreasonably withhold consent to a Customer assignment for which consent is required.
elements.evidence: The opening mutual consent provision states that the required consent will not be unreasonably withheld.

elements.element: Vendor assignments other than assignments to a successor are permitted subject to Customer consent.
elements.evidence: Although the general provision permits assignments with consent, Contractor assignments to Company competitors are prohibited absolutely and cannot be authorized by consent.

elements.element: Customer may not unreasonably withhold consent to a Vendor assignment for which consent is required.
elements.evidence: The opening mutual consent provision states that the required consent will not be unreasonably withheld.

result.reason: The operative language satisfies every preferred requirement, but not the fallback's mutual successor-assignment structure. It is not minimal because it additionally grants Company a reorganization assignment right, imposes written notice on Company assignments, and bars suspension and repricing following a Company change of control—none of which is necessary to complete the preferred position. The clause otherwise preserves the original consent framework without contradiction. Drafting quality score: 8/10. The language is clear and internally workable, though “competitor” is undefined and the added terms exceed the requested preferred position.
